chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Dawud ibn Abi Yazid al-Attar from some of our companions, he said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Beware of looking, for it is an arrow from the arrows of Iblis.' And he said: 'There is no harm in looking at what the clothes are placed upon (i.e., the body parts covered by clothing).'

key_terms.سَهْمٌ مِنْ سِهَامِ إِبْلِيسَ: An arrow from the arrows of Iblis (metaphor for temptation)
key_terms.مَا وُضِعَتِ اَلثِّيَابُ: What the clothes are placed upon (covered body parts)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between forbidden looking and permissible looking before marriage in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the general gaze of desire, which he metaphorically calls an 'arrow of Iblis,' and the permissible examination of a prospective bride's physical attributes prior to marriage. This ruling provides the jurisprudential basis for the practice of *nazar al-khitbah*, allowing men to view the parts of a woman covered by her outer garment (*thi'ab*) to ensure compatibility, while maintaining modesty and avoiding excessive scrutiny.
